methodological_notes.isolated_population_definition: Population of cut-off zones (100,310) represents all residents residing in hydraulically severed settlement zones who cannot access emergency shelters by road. Of these, 38,481 residents live directly within flooded pixels (exposed population).
methodological_notes.cropland_waterlogging_limitation: Cropland flooded or waterlogged (8,170 ha): rice paddies and low-lying agricultural fields may naturally hold water or be waterlogged, creating radar backscatter signatures overlapping with floodwater.
methodological_notes.boundary_truncation_warning: Results are within the Cachar study window ([92.70, 24.75, 92.90, 24.90]); roads leaving the window are truncated, so cut-off zones near the edge may be overstated. 10 of 20 settlement zones touch the window perimeter (5 cut off, 5 connected).
methodological_notes.roads_buffer_assumption: Roads potentially cut (196.4 km): derived by applying a 50m spatial safety buffer around flood polygons. Limitation: bridges, flyovers, and elevated embankments are not explicitly modelled due to lack of elevation tags in OSM.

provenance.flood_impact_metrics: DERIVED (U-Net ResNet34 spatial overlay in UTM Zone 46N)
